title: Fundamental principles of the Federative Republic (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Brazil’s Constitution opens with sovereignty, citizenship, dignity of the human person, social values of labour and enterprise, and political pluralism. These principles guide interpretation of rights and state organisation.

title: Individual & collective rights (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Title II enumerates rights and duties spanning life, liberty, equality, privacy, expression, assembly, political participation, workers’ protections, and social rights. Many clauses interact with ordinary legislation and programmes.

title: Union, states, Federal District, municipalities (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: legislative competences are divided among Union, states, DF, and municipalities with residual rules. Taxing powers and transfers are constitutionally structured, affecting public services and enforcement.

title: Public Prosecutor’s Office & defence of legal order (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the Ministério Público has institutional roles promoting justice and defending diffuse and collective interests as defined by law, distinct from private prosecution or counsel functions.
